agencies that were targeted by DOGE. (Photo by </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/f481d2c7-5ed9-41e5-990d-b128a784b68d?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="text-decoration: underline;">Samuel Corum</a><span> via Getty Images)</span></figcaption></figure></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>I read </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/674f0bda-e138-4d68-81ea-b7b9b926d020?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">Rachel Carson’s classic, “Silent Spring,” recently</a><span>, and while it contains plenty of the </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/6dec405c-834a-4f02-bbfd-7b372cb6bdfb?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">neopastoral ideas</a><span> that animate the environmental movement (ideas I broadly disagree with), it also features eco-modernist tendencies. The most striking of these is her brief discussion of a then-new idea for dealing with a cattle pest called the New World screwworm. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">The main thrust of the book is that spraying insecticides everywhere is bad. But she mentions that basically everyone agrees that spraying is not a good screwworm solution, because even in places with big screwworm issues there’s not that much bug density. An alternative approach is to raise in captivity a bunch of male screwworms that are then dosed with radiation that renders them sterile. If you flood an area with sterilized males, they out-compete the wild males for access to females and the size of the next generation is greatly reduced. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Carson is enthusiastic about this initiative that she says worked well in Florida and, at the time she wrote the book, is being utilized in an attempt to eradicate the screwworm from the southeastern United States. She suggests that maybe someday it could be expanded to Texas as well, though Texas would be harder because it would always be at risk of re-infiltration from Mexico. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>This program proved even more successful than Carson imagined. Not only was the screwworm eliminated from the southwestern United States (</span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/ebaea16d-5072-4fb6-8860-c9f07a8f9859?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">a way bigger deal than the Southeast</a><span>), but from Mexico and Central America as well. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">A screwworm barrier was eventually established in southern Panama, a much more defensible frontier, and for decades the screwworm was kept far away from the United States of America. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>But this spring in the United States, we’re seeing the </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/9d05086a-9eb1-4ce1-9e36-5ae2fd5030d8?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">first screwworm cases in cattle since the 1960s</a><span>. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>We also had 2,288 cases of measles last year, the most since 1991, and </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/dee3b8b4-7dbb-4c81-8464-673d39cd8933?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">there have been 2,030 cases so far in 2026</a><span> — and it’s only June. As a result, America’s status as a country that </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/647e323f-14d3-48c2-bf7a-976cc9341c2b?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">has eliminated measles is under review</a><span>. Meanwhile, the </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/4911058b-9c5f-4db8-aeba-f8509ee6c1f0?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">Ebola outbreak raging in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo</a><span> is on pace to be the biggest on record. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">None of this is “Donald Trump’s fault” in the sense that the spike in global energy prices resulting from his misguided war in the Middle East is his fault. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">But with all three issues, his irresponsible policy decisions have made the situation worse. They’re not direct cause-effect fiascos like the Strait of Hormuz, but subtler areas in which sloppiness, erosion of state capacity, naive individualism, and a zero-sum mindset have left the world worse off and jeopardized American interests. </p><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.125em * 1);">The screwworm saga</h4><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>The breakdown of screwworm containment started, ironically, right around the time that </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/be956d33-ee07-4fea-9837-2bb6011630ea?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">Sarah Zhang’s profile of the barrier operation in Panama</a><span> brought new attention to the success of the program. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Zhang’s piece came out in May 2020, just as the Covid pandemic disrupted operations at the facility in Panama where they breed and drop the sterile flies, causing countermeasures to wobble. The pandemic also disrupted surveillance efforts. And in 2021–22, a surge of people began crossing the Darién Gap to try to make asylum claims in the United States — creating a chaotic situation in which it was harder to guard against cattle-smuggling. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">By 2023, the successful barrier was breaking down. </p><div class="paywall-jump" data-component-name="PaywallToDOM" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;display: none;"></div><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>To try to get a handle on the problem, the Biden administration tapped Commodity Credit Corporation funding in </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/ab89da0d-586f-4279-9280-1ac557804969?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">2023</a><span> and </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8309ac8f-8b62-45ae-9359-e92e4e9c72d8?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">2024</a><span> to provide additional resources for the </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/82887172-a134-4cba-850c-a1e0d7ffaadd?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service</a><span>. They also </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/aff66536-9a64-4e78-84b2-e0ff7a6830ab?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">requested funding from Congress</a><span> to upgrade the facility in Panama where the sterilized flies are bred. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>In early 2025, a bipartisan group of members of Congress </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/18216b8f-8468-4547-9f24-581673922ee3?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">wrote to the then-new Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins</a><span> asking her to establish a new breeding facility in the United States. Sterile screwworms used to be bred in Texas, but the eradication program had advanced far enough that the whole thing had shifted to Panama. The members thought, rightly, that with containment wobbling it didn’t make sense to continue relying exclusively on Panama. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Instead, as part of DOGE’s dismantling of USAID, the Trump administration </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/8a1a12a9-e5c2-4eaf-bc48-ed0770d097e0?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">canceled contracts to fund monitoring of the screwworm</a><span>, bird flu, and other diseases. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>To avoid scolding by fact-checkers, you’re supposed to be clear that these were </span><em>not</em><span> cuts to the core production and dissemination of the sterile flies, just to the surveillance. But </span><em>of course</em><span> surveillance is an important part of containment. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Trump could have easily blamed the re-infection of Central America on the Biden administration’s immigration policy and dedicated himself to fixing the problem. Instead, countermeasures were weakened by his hasty attacks on USAID. Meanwhile, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service was </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/1bc27316-340d-410e-92dc-e18d3971a344?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">hit by chaotic layoffs</a><span>. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>In early 2025, the price of eggs was a highly salient political issue and people were talking a lot about bird flu, so it was embarrassing to the administration that they had fired people who were working on bird flu. </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/668a781b-6a41-4784-b6c8-858a692336aa?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">Those people largely got re-hired</a><span>. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">At the time, though, New World screwworm wasn’t a big topic of conversation, so things just marched on. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">And I would say that one of several basic conceptual problems with DOGE’s approach is that whether someone is working on an issue that happens to be politically salient right now is not really a good way to assess the objective importance of a public-sector function. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">DOGE is not the whole cause of the screwworm outbreak, but the situation is emblematic of an irresponsible approach to government where everything is driven by news cycles and short-term reactions to the stock market rather than understanding what’s going on. </p><h4 class="header-anchor-post" optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.125em * 1);">Waning pandemic preparedness</h4><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>The 2014 Ebola outbreak became a big deal during that year’s midterm elections because Republicans cynically exploited it and because media coverage at the time was completely insane. It was a </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/151997e9-d043-4360-9e8b-907a446a5cfb?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">huge story that fall</a><span>, only to disappear as soon as Republicans </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/099e848b-6860-4994-89b3-8dad4bb20f19?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">won a bunch</a><span> of Senate seats. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>After all, nothing actually </span><em>happened</em><span> in America related to Ebola. Republicans insisted that it was incredibly dangerous to allow American health-care workers to receive treatment in the United States, but actually that turned out to be fine. The United States </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/7723f699-f41d-4125-98c9-44e732477643?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">led a successful response to contain the outbreak</a><span>, and soon after the world </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/bc0b64b9-ff12-4aff-9a35-644cc64f4e5c?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">developed an Ebola vaccine</a><span> that unfortunately does not work against this strain. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Now there appears to be an even larger outbreak, but the Trump administration’s focus is almost entirely on quarantine. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>They want to set up a </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/b0c8bfdd-1616-47c5-bd16-6a3304827cca?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">special Americans-only treatment center in Kenya</a><span> that will allow the U.S. government to show special consideration for sick U.S. citizens without bringing them back home. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">But the risk of Ebola spreading to the United States isn’t really that a health professional working in the region will come home for treatment and escape quarantine. It’s that the more the virus spreads in Africa, the more opportunities there are for it to come into the United States through some channel that’s not being monitored. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>What the administration has done to address that so far is to ban people who were in (or passed through) Congo, Uganda, or South Sudan within 21 days of their planned travel to the United States. And now they’re </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/78439e32-cd54-453e-bcd8-3e2dbdd54048?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">telling European governments that they should impose the same travel restrictions</a><span> as the United States in advance of what’s expected to be a lot of Europeans coming here for the World Cup. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Travel restrictions clearly </span><em>can</em><span> be a useful tool for fighting an epidemic. But as we’ve seen before, even a very migration-skeptical Trump administration doesn’t want to impose travel restrictions that carry significant economic costs. Three very poor countries in central Africa can be cut off easily, but we want those European soccer fans. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>Ultimately, the best way to keep everyone safe is going to be to actually help with the situation in Africa. But America’s ability to do that is greatly impaired by </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/0b745eac-ac40-4f8a-bee1-89484e008978?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">cuts to USAID</a><span> and </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/d7ddfe3f-2d98-410c-bd0c-40ca132268c6?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">to the C.D.C.</a><span>, cuts that were once again inflicted by DOGE. </span></p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;">Here, again, it’s not “Trump’s fault” that there is an Ebola outbreak. Stuff happens. </p><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>But just as I </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/b059e45a-1d8c-4ff4-af19-57d4ffbb7ba2?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">wrote during the hantavirus scare back in May</a><span>, the structural issue is that pandemic risk is growing globally thanks to a larger, less-poor population and better technology. Under the circumstances, we need to be making prudent investments in prevention. The Trump approach of cutting things that nobody notices in the short term is the exact opposite of that.</span></p><h4 class="header-anchor-post" style="position: relative;font-family: 'SF Pro Display',-apple-system-headline,system-ui,-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,Helvetica,Arial,sans-serif,'Apple Color Emoji','Segoe UI Emoji','Segoe UI Symbol';font-weight: bold;-webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased;-moz-osx-font-smoothing: antialiased;-webkit-appearance: optimizelegibility;-moz-appearance: optimizelegibility;appearance: optimizelegibility;margin: 1em 0 0.625em 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 1.16em;font-size: calc(1.125em * 1);">Waning vaccination rates</h4><p style="margin: 0 0 20px 0;color: rgb(54,55,55);line-height: 26px;font-size: 16px;"><span>The American public sector used to maintain a high level of vaccine coverage against common childhood illnesses to prevent outbreaks. But now, most states’ childhood vaccination rates </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/aee3c9c3-9199-46ea-a12a-de3bf2da9d3c?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">have dropped</a><span> beneath the robust-herd-immunity threshold </span><a href="https://substack.com/redirect/21175eb6-e06b-4f42-8564-442c9e1b9f33?j=eyJ1IjoiNHd4eHhhIn0.THiPlOhlJVrM95bfyrnJXrugnT66pFY3JaSTi-_WlgE" style="color: #04b2a5;text-decoration: none;">for measles</a><span>, leaving us structurally vulnerable to new outbreaks.</span></p><div class="captioned-image-container-static" style="font-size: 16px;line-height: 26px;margin: 32px auto;"><figure
